newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedbank takes 9.1 percent stake in new HSB bank.
newsitem.headline: Swedbank takes 9.1 percent stake in new HSB bank.

text.p: One of Sweden's big four banks, Swedbank, Tuesday grabbed a slice of newcomer HSB Bank in the continued restructuring of the Swedish banking sector.

Swedbank said it intended to pay 52 million crowns ($6.5 million) for a 9.1 percent stake in HSB Bank, a banking unit of cooperative real estate company HSB Sverige AB that will begin operating in October.

Swedbank said it would buy the stake by subscribing for stock in a new issue. It has a conditional call option for a further 3.4 percent stake in HSB Bank, which will be a bank for cooperative apartments.
"Swedbank and HSB have had a close cooperation for many years," said Swedbank, adding that it was a natural development to take a stake in HSB Bank
The two banks will cooperate on clearing, technical operations, fund operations and first mortgages.
"It's not such a big deal but it shows that players are talking to each other," Fredrik Myren, analyst at HSBC James Capel, told Reuters.
"The groups have been cooperating and they have the same philosophy -- they both have a very popular profile."
The deal is the latest reshuffle in the Swedish banking sector as banks prepare to meet fearsome international competition ahead of Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) beginning Jan. 1, 1999.
In addition, mergers and cooperation can trim information technology costs because the banks have to update computer systems anyway ahead of both monetary union and the turn of the century.
